title: Caves of Qud: Diaspora 开创先河，成为 Steam 首个以抢先体验形式发行的 DLC

Caves of Qud: Diaspora is the first early access DLC on Steam

Caves of Qud: Diaspora breaks new ground by being the first early access DLC release on Steam
The roguelike RPG is no longer in Steam Early Access, but its upcoming DLC Diaspora will be, marking untrodden ground for the in-development program.
Imran Khan
,
Contributing Editor
October 15, 2026
schedule
3 Min Read
Image via Freehold Games/Kitfox Games
Caves of Qud
has been in some form of development since 2007 when Freehold Games began development on it. It didn't hit Steam Early Access, the PC gaming store's program for letting in-development games be sold and shaped with community feedback, until 2015, and then spent roughly nine years doing that until a 1.0 release in 2024.
But
Caves of Qud
is, in a form, coming back to Early Access through its new DLC titled
Diaspora
, which is a first for Steam.
Generally when a game leaves the Early Access program, it's akin to a graduation.
Caves of Qud
bringing new content back to the model has not been done before. It is unclear if there were specific rules prohibiting this or if simply no one ever thought to do it, but DLC content usually just launches in a 1.0 state.
"I was a bit hesitant at first to be honest,"
Kitfox Games
co-founder and head of publishing Tanya X. Short tells Game Developer. "But Jason [Grinblat] and Brian [Bucklew] were really keen to continue with the development strategy that had been so successful for the main game throughout their long Early Access."

Short points out that Valve, owner and maintainer of Steam, has been a supportive partner in these uncharted waters. Apparently the company had to make a "manual adjustment" in Steam's backend to "enable it as an option."
"Their store page review then flagged it as a bug," she added.
It's unusual to release DLC expansions officially in Early Access
Freehold's official statement on why it is choosing early access for Diaspora is rather candid. In a press statement, the studio states "One,
Caves of Qud
is an extremely complicated game with many interlocking systems & features and lots of unpredictable, emergent gameplay. Diaspora will add a whole new layer to that. Just like with the base game, our approach to building something this complex is to have the community stress test it the whole way.
"Two,
Caves of Qud
development is slow. It takes a long time and a lot of love to hit the quality bar we set for ourselves. We don't want to be beholden to a timeline that forces us to compromise the expansion's vision. And so, by working in Early Access, we're able to fund Diaspora's development as it happens, watering the flower as it blooms."
It is unclear how well this plan will play out, just as it's difficult to foresee how anything new will play out. But just as
Caves of Qud
hopped on to the Early Access program relatively nascently into its rollout, the title is perhaps leading the charge again for developers that may be keeping an eye out for new communication and development models for extra content.

Report: Steam now requires Australian users to verify their age with credit cards
"[Brian and Jason] love working with their players, and they already had all the processes and habits to do it again, so why not?" says Short when asked why she agreed to pursue this novel idea. "It would have been uncomfortable and against their natures to work in a totally closed-room environment, rather than develop alongside feedback from their players."
